title: GPU & CPU Accelerated ML Inference Server with Dynamic Batching
problem: Serving machine learning models in production under heavy concurrent traffic creates severe hardware bottlenecks and spiraling infrastructure costs. Sequential request evaluation underutilizes parallel compute cores, while naive batching introduces prohibitive latency penalties for single requests. This project constructs an accelerated machine learning inference server in Python, PyTorch, CUDA, and FastAPI. The engine implements a dynamic batching queue with configurable microsecond timeout windows, INT8 and FP16 quantization to reduce memory bandwidth demands, asynchronous request worker pools, and an automatic CPU fallback engine using ONNX Runtime for hardware portability on standard developer laptops.
use_cases: High-throughput microservice backends serving deep learning embedding models under strict latency SLAs
Cost-optimized inference infrastructure maximizing throughput per compute core or GPU instance
Edge deployment platforms executing quantized neural networks across heterogeneous CPU/GPU hardware
hard_parts: Coalescing asynchronous concurrent HTTP requests into unified dynamic batch tensors within microsecond timeout windows
Calibrating post-training INT8 quantization to compress model size without degrading classification accuracy
Managing GPU device memory buffers and host-to-device transfers to prevent out-of-memory crashes during traffic surges
Architecting seamless CPU fallback using ONNX Runtime execution providers when CUDA devices are absent
screener_signals: Modular Python codebase separating dynamic batching schedulers, quantization pipelines, and FastAPI serving endpoints
High-concurrency load benchmark demonstrating greater than 2.8x throughput increase via dynamic batching over sequential execution
Anti-fake verification script issuing concurrent bursts and proving tensor dimension batching inside model forward execution

components.name: Dynamic Batching Queue & Scheduler
components.purpose: Accumulates incoming requests across microsecond timeout windows and coalesces them into single tensor batches

components.name: Model Quantization & Optimization Engine
components.purpose: Quantizes neural network weights to INT8 and FP16 precision, reducing memory footprint and latency

components.name: Hardware Execution & CPU Fallback Engine
components.purpose: Dispatches tensor batches to CUDA streams when available, falling back seamlessly to ONNX CPU execution

components.name: FastAPI High-Concurrency Inference Gateway
components.purpose: Accepts client inference requests asynchronously, dispatching promises that resolve upon batch completion

architecture.data_flow: Client inference requests arrive at the FastAPI gateway; requests enter the Dynamic Batching Queue; the scheduler monitors batch size and timeout windows; once threshold or timeout triggers, inputs concatenate into a single batch tensor; the Hardware Execution Engine runs model forward pass on CUDA or CPU; the batch tensor slices into individual output responses; FastAPI resolves promises and returns individual prediction payloads to clients in under 25 milliseconds.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Bounded queue capacities preventing out-of-memory exhaustion during traffic surges; timeout thresholds capping individual request latency.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an accelerated ML inference server in Python/PyTorch with dynamic batching, INT8 quantization, and CPU fallback.
worksheet.q2: Target users: ML systems engineers, AI platform architects, and performance engineers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: deep learning embedding services, cost-optimized inference clusters, and edge neural network serving.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 39 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 34 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 39.1 -> 39 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: microsecond dynamic batch scheduling, INT8 quantization calibration, GPU memory buffer management, and seamless ONNX CPU fallback.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: pretrained PyTorch model weights (~45MB) with 1,000 labeled test samples. Open-source weights only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only (GPU optional), $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: ONNX Runtime CPU mode.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Latency spikes on low traffic from batch starvation. Fallback: 5ms microsecond timeout dispatch.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: sequential loops masquerading as batching. Anti-fake check 5 sends 8 concurrent requests and asserts forward batch size equals 8.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; standard open-source vision/text models only.
